title: Goodbye in Polish: Do Widzenia, Na Razie, Pa and Dobranoc
excerpt: Goodbye in Polish is do widzenia for anyone you'd call Pan or Pani, and cześć, na razie or pa for friends. Pronunciation and usage tips.
metaDescription: Goodbye in Polish is do widzenia formally and cześć, na razie or pa with friends. Learn pronunciation, good night in Polish, phone sign-offs and etiquette.
summary: Do widzenia (doh vee-DZEH-nyah) is the polite goodbye for anyone you'd address as Pan or Pani; with friends, use cześć, na razie, pa or trzymaj się.
Phrases like do jutra and do poniedziałku put the noun in the genitive, and on the phone the goodbye becomes do usłyszenia.
Good night in Polish is dobranoc, and bedtime wishes include słodkich snów and the very Polish kolorowych snów (colourful dreams).
The wish is always miłego wieczoru, never miłego wieczora, and żegnam can sound cold, so learners should stick with do widzenia.
featuredImageAlt: A family waving goodbye as a train pulls away from the station, one of the most common moments to say goodbye in Polish
authorBio: PolishPal Contributor writes about Polish culture, history, and language for learners and the Polish diaspora.
factNotes: The 'miłego dnia is English-inspired' and 'żegnam is stylistically marked / do widzenia is the neutral farewell' points come from wartowiedziec.pl summarising Andrzej Markowski (secondary source), so they are attributed to 'an etiquette guide drawing on Markowski'. That same source calls do zobaczenia 'rarer and more official', which I did not repeat; the text only says it is slightly warmer and usable in both registers. The two-word spelling 'na razie' is supported by the PWN search page linking to poradnia answers titled 'na razie czy narazie?' and 'Pisownia na razie musi zostać' (answer text not opened); note the live post learn-polish-with-netflix lists the misspelling 'narazie' as a separate phrase. The claim that the threshold superstition also applies to farewells comes from search summaries of Babbel/3seaseurope (not opened directly), so it is stated briefly without statistics. 'Do napisania' is labelled colloquial from general knowledge.
